clues: This town sits on the north coast of Tenerife. It lies in the north west part of that island.
Trade winds push a sea of clouds to this island. The clouds bring extra water for a thirsty green woodland.
Its name was first written in 1509. Farm growth meant new grain stores had to be built.
Leafy woods stand out next to dry coast plains. The sharp contrast in green growth is hard to miss.
This place lies at the heart of the Teno Massif. It is prized for its rich plant and animal life.
